newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian court officials sent for trial.
newsitem.headline: Italian court officials sent for trial.

text.p: The president of Italy's Court of Accounts, which oversees state accounts, and three of its magistrates were ordered on Friday to stand trial for alleged abuse of office and false statements.

A Rome appeals court, overturning a 1995 ruling to drop the case, ordered Court of Accounts president Giuseppe Carbone and magistrates Emidio di Giambattista, Roberto Coltelli and Sergio Ristuccia to stand trial on May 14.

Carbone, accused of abuse of office, is suspected of not properly informing authorities that while serving as head of the court he was also president of Cemat, a company belonging to the state-run railway Ferrovie dello Stato.
Di Giambattista and Rustuccia are accused of making false statements to officials about Carbone's position with Cemat.

Coltelli is accused of failing to investigate a possible conflict of interest in 1998 when former Rome mayor Franco Carraro was both president of the Italian Olympic Committee and the national soccer federation's extraordinary commissioner.
The Court of Accounts has supervisory jurisdiction over the accounts of both state entities.
